title: The House of the Seven Gables — What Science Actually Says #Shorts
description:
Strip The House of the Seven Gables of its poetry and the mechanism underneath is stranger. The House of the Seven Gables: A Romance is a Gothic novel written beginning in mid-1850 by American author Nathaniel Hawthorne and published in April 1851 by Ticknor and Fields of Boston. In the book, Hawthorne explores themes of guilt, retribution, and atonement, and colors the tale with suggestions of the supernatural and witchcraft.

Nihilism is not the conclusion of The House of the Seven Gables — it is the floor you stand on while examining it. Also, Clifford was well aware of Holgrave's true identity, and the two are working together to settle the score with Jaffrey. The novel was adapted to a 60-minute television production in 1960 for The Shirley Temple Show with Shirley Temple as Phoebe, Robert Culp as Holgrave, Agnes Moorehead as Hepzibah, and Martin Landau as Clifford.
